hook: Sanjay Ghemawat earned an SB from Cornell University in 1987 and a PhD in computer science from MIT in 1995, advised by Barbara Liskov and Frans Kaashoek. Before joining Google in late 1999 he worked as a member of the research staff at Digital Equipment Corporation's Systems Research Center in Palo Alto. At Google he became one of the principal architects of the distributed systems that made the company's scale possible, co-designing the Google File System in 2003, MapReduce with Jeff Dean in 2004, Bigtable in 2006, and Spanner, Google's globally distributed database, in 2012. He has also contributed to Protocol Buffers, LevelDB, TensorFlow, and the Pathways distributed machine learning system. He now holds the title of Senior Fellow at Google, among the company's most senior technical positions, and has spent more than two decades building the infrastructure layer underneath Google's products and, later, its large-scale AI training systems.

quick_facts: Senior Fellow at Google, where he has worked since 1999
Earned a PhD in computer science from MIT, advised by Barbara Liskov and Frans Kaashoek
Co-authored the 2003 paper introducing the Google File System, a foundation of large-scale distributed storage
Co-created MapReduce with Jeff Dean in 2004, a programming model that popularized large-scale parallel data processing
Co-designed Bigtable (2006) and Spanner (2012), Google's distributed structured storage and globally distributed database systems
Elected to the National Academy of Engineering in 2009 and the American Academy of Arts and Sciences in 2016

achievements.title: Google File System (2003)
achievements.impact: Co-designed with Howard Gobioff and Shun-Tak Leung, GFS became the storage layer underlying Google's search index and many later systems, and its design influenced the open-source Hadoop Distributed File System.

achievements.title: MapReduce (2004)
achievements.impact: Co-created with Jeff Dean, MapReduce gave engineers a simple model for processing huge datasets across thousands of machines and became a template for large-scale data processing across the industry.

achievements.title: Bigtable (2006)
achievements.impact: Co-designed Google's distributed structured storage system, built to scale to petabytes of data across thousands of commodity servers and later open influence on systems like Apache HBase.

achievements.title: Spanner (2012)
achievements.impact: Co-designed Google's globally distributed, strongly consistent database, which underpins services used by billions of people and later influenced the design of Google's Cloud Spanner product.
